Hydrologic Outlook issued September 19 at 11:59AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY

ESFRIW

Periods of showers and thunderstorms are expected across the northern
half of Wyoming Saturday and Sunday as a wet weather system shifts
east across the state. This weather system is funneling abundant
tropical moisture into northern and eastern portions of the state
with it's eastward progression. Given the high moisture content, many
thunderstorms could feature heavy rainfall and possibly lead to
localized flooding. Poor drainage areas, urban areas, and steep
terrain will be the most susceptible locations for this isolated
flooding.

Many locations could see an additional 0.5" to 1.25" of rain through
Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling quickly in
thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

Flood Watch issued September 19 at 2:52AM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK

A series of low pressures will move through the panhandle this
weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing levels to
increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy rainfall and
associated runoff will produce significant river rises with the
potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway, White Pass, And Haines.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the rain will continue this evening into Saturday before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday into Sunday.
Between the two systems, the flow is expected to remain onshore
keeping moisture moving into the area.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.

Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK

ESFAFC

High water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next
few days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water
levels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of
next week.

Locations:

* Communities across the lower Kuskokwim River and its tributaries,
including, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,
Napaskiak, Napkiak, Kasigluk, Nunapitchuk, and Atmauluak.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* High water in the Kuskokwim and other area rivers (e.g. Kwethluk
River, Johnson River, etc) may inundate low-lying areas in the
aforementioned communities, nearby fish camps, and other lowlands.

Details/Analysis [What's causing this?]:

* Rainfall: The Kuskokwim River basin, from the mouth at Kuskokwim
Bay upstream to the headwaters in the Alaska Range and Kilbuck
Mountains, has received approximately 150 to 200 percent of normal
rainfall this summer (June to August). These rains have continued
into September, with nearly the entire basin near or exceeding 200
percent of rainfall, with much of that rainfall occurring over the
last few days.

* Persistent High Water: This heavy rainfall has resulted in
anomalously high water levels being routed down from the Upper
Kuskokwim to the Lower Kuskokwim. The river gages at McGrath and
Crooked Creek are near or exceeding record levels for this time of
year. The water levels at these stations have crested in the last
week, suggesting that the water inflow to the lower Kuskokwim
Communities may be on the decrease soon.

* Compounding Factors: In addition to the recent rainfall and
elevated river levels, strong coastal winds brought several feet of
surge to the coast, causing elevated water levels near the mouth of
the Kuskokwim River. This effectively reduces the slope of the
river, slowing drainage and resulting in water becoming backed up.

* Forecast Thoughts: A shift in the weather pattern will bring
conditions favorable for water levels to decrease. Northerly winds
will increase Saturday and continue into early next week to 20 to
30 kt, with higher gusts possible at times, and bring cooler and
drier air to the region. Precipitation will be sparse and generally
light. Additionally, tidal models indicate a slight negative surge
along the coast due to the multi-day period of strong northerly
winds, potentially assisting drainage of water from the lower
Kuskokwim River.

Look Ahead:

* After a period of weather conditions favorable for receding water,
confidence is growing that another strong Bering Sea storm will
affect western Alaska late next week (Sept 23-26). A return to
southerly winds and higher coastal water in conjunction to heavy
rainfall may exacerbate river conditions once again, particularly
on the smaller tributaries such as the Kwethluk and Johnson Rivers.
However, details remain uncertain at this time as confidence is low
in storm track and intensity. Fortunately, natural tidal cycles in
Bethel and the rest of the lower Kuskokwim favor lower tides than
usual for this timeframe which may offset any additional water or
surge.
